# tower - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower/*/tower/index.html

## Expand description

`async fn(Request) -> Result<Response, Error>`

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Tower is a library of modular and reusable components for building robust networking clients and servers.

Tower provides a simple core abstraction, the [ Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) trait, which
represents an asynchronous function taking a request and returning either a
response or an error. This abstraction can be used to model both clients and
servers.

Generic components, like [ timeout](https://docs.rs/timeout/index.html),

[rate limiting](https://docs.rs/limit/rate/index.html), and

[load balancing](https://docs.rs/balance/index.html), can be modeled as

[s that wrap some inner service and apply additional behavior before or after the inner service is called. This allows implementing these components in a protocol-agnostic, composable way. Typically, such services are referred to as](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`*middleware*.

An additional abstraction, the [ Layer](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html) trait, is used to compose
middleware with

[s. If a](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[can be thought of as an asynchronous function from a request type to a response type, a](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[is a function taking a](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[of one type and returning a](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[of a different type. The](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[type is used to add middleware to a service by composing it with multiple](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceBuilder.html)

`ServiceBuilder`[s.](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[§](https://docs.rs#the-tower-ecosystem)The Tower Ecosystem

Tower is made up of the following crates:

- `tower`
- `tower-service`
- `tower-layer`
- `tower-test`

Since the [ Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) and

[traits are important integration points for all libraries using Tower, they are kept as stable as possible, and breaking changes are made rarely. Therefore, they are defined in separate crates,](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[and](https://crates.io/crates/tower-service)

`tower-service`[. This crate contains re-exports of those core traits, implementations of commonly-used middleware, and](https://crates.io/crates/tower-layer)

`tower-layer`[utilities](https://docs.rs/trait.ServiceExt.html)for working with

[s and](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[s. Finally, the](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[crate provides tools for testing programs using Tower.](https://crates.io/crates/tower-test)

`tower-test`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Tower provides an abstraction layer, and generic implementations of various
middleware. This means that the `tower` crate on its own does *not* provide
a working implementation of a network client or server. Instead, Tower’s
[ Service trait](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) provides an integration point between
application code, libraries providing middleware implementations, and
libraries that implement servers and/or clients for various network
protocols.

Depending on your particular use case, you might use Tower in several ways:

-
**Implementing application logic**for a networked program. You might use the`Service`[provided by this crate](https://docs.rs#modules)and by other libraries to add functionality to clients and servers provided by one or more protocol implementations.
-
**Implementing middleware**to add custom behavior to network clients and servers in a reusable manner. This might be general-purpose middleware (and if it is, please consider releasing your middleware as a library for other Tower users!) or application-specific behavior that needs to be shared between multiple clients or servers.
-
**Implementing a network protocol**. Libraries that implement network protocols (such as HTTP) can depend on`tower-service`to use the`Service``Service``Service`Additionally, when a network protocol requires functionality already provided by existing Tower middleware, a protocol implementation might use Tower middleware internally, as well as as an integration point.

[§](https://docs.rs#library-support)Library Support

A number of third-party libraries support Tower and the [ Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) trait.
The following is an incomplete list of such libraries:

- `hyper`
- `tonic`- [gRPC-over-HTTP/2](https://grpc.io)implementation built on top of- `hyper`- [here](https://github.com/hyperium/tonic/tree/master/examples/src/tower)for examples of using- `tonic`
- `warp`- [here](https://docs.rs/warp/0.2.5/warp/fn.service.html)for details on using- `warp`
- `tower-lsp`- [Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/)based on Tower.

If you’re the maintainer of a crate that supports Tower, we’d love to add
your crate to this list! Please [open a PR](https://github.com/tower-rs/tower/compare) adding a brief description of
your library!

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting Started

If you’re brand new to Tower and want to start with the basics, we recommend you
check out some of our [guides](https://github.com/tower-rs/tower/tree/master/guides).

The various middleware implementations provided by this crate are feature flagged, so that users can only compile the parts of Tower they need. By default, all the optional middleware are disabled.

To get started using all of Tower’s optional middleware, add this to your
`Cargo.toml`:

`tower = { version = "0.4", features = ["full"] }`Alternatively, you can only enable some features. For example, to enable
only the [ retry](https://docs.rs/retry/index.html) and

[middleware, write:](https://docs.rs/timeout/index.html)

`timeout``tower = { version = "0.4", features = ["retry", "timeout"] }`See [here](https://docs.rs#modules) for a complete list of all middleware provided by
Tower.

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-rust-versions)Supported Rust Versions

Tower will keep a rolling MSRV (minimum supported Rust version) policy of **at
least** 6 months. When increasing the MSRV, the new Rust version must have been
released at least six months ago. The current MSRV is 1.64.0.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [balance](https://docs.rs/balance/index.html)- `balance`
- Middleware that allows balancing load among multiple services.
- [buffer](https://docs.rs/buffer/index.html)- `buffer`
- Middleware that provides a buffered mpsc channel to a service.
- [builder](https://docs.rs/builder/index.html)
- Builder types to compose layers and services
- [discover](https://docs.rs/discover/index.html)- `discover`
- Service discovery
- [filter](https://docs.rs/filter/index.html)- `filter`
- Conditionally dispatch requests to the inner service based on the result of a predicate.
- [hedge](https://docs.rs/hedge/index.html)- `hedge`
- Pre-emptively retry requests which have been outstanding for longer than a given latency percentile.
- [layer](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html)
- A collection of `Layer`
- [limit](https://docs.rs/limit/index.html)- `limit`
- Tower middleware for limiting requests.
- [load](https://docs.rs/load/index.html)- `load`
- Service load measurement
- [load_](https://docs.rs/load_shed/index.html)- shed - `load-shed`
- Middleware for shedding load when inner services aren’t ready.
- [make](https://docs.rs/make/index.html)- `make`
- Trait aliases for Services that produce specific types of Responses.
- [ready_](https://docs.rs/ready_cache/index.html)- cache - `ready-cache`
- A cache of services
- [reconnect](https://docs.rs/reconnect/index.html)- `reconnect`
- Reconnect services when they fail.
- [retry](https://docs.rs/retry/index.html)- `retry`
- Middleware for retrying “failed” requests.
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/spawn_ready/index.html)- ready - `spawn-ready`
- When an underlying service is not ready, drive it to readiness on a background task.
- [steer](https://docs.rs/steer/index.html)- `steer`
- This module provides functionality to aid managing routing requests between `Service`
- [timeout](https://docs.rs/timeout/index.html)- `timeout`
- Middleware that applies a timeout to requests.
- [util](https://docs.rs/util/index.html)- `util`
- Various utility types and functions that are generally used with Tower.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

# tower_service/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)#![warn(
[2](https://docs.rs#2)    missing_debug_implementations,
[3](https://docs.rs#3)    missing_docs,
[4](https://docs.rs#4)    rust_2018_idioms,
[5](https://docs.rs#5)    unreachable_pub
[6](https://docs.rs#6))]
[7](https://docs.rs#7)#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
[8](https://docs.rs#8)// `rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links` is checked on CI
[9](https://docs.rs#9)
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! Definition of the core `Service` trait to Tower
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! The [`Service`] trait provides the necessary abstractions for defining
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! request / response clients and servers. It is simple but powerful and is
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! used as the foundation for the rest of Tower.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)
[16](https://docs.rs#16)use std::future::Future;
[17](https://docs.rs#17)use std::task::{Context, Poll};
[18](https://docs.rs#18)
[19](https://docs.rs#19)/// An asynchronous function from a `Request` to a `Response`.
[20](https://docs.rs#20)///
[21](https://docs.rs#21)/// The `Service` trait is a simplified interface making it easy to write
[22](https://docs.rs#22)/// network applications in a modular and reusable way, decoupled from the
[23](https://docs.rs#23)/// underlying protocol. It is one of Tower's fundamental abstractions.
[24](https://docs.rs#24)///
[25](https://docs.rs#25)/// # Functional
[26](https://docs.rs#26)///
[27](https://docs.rs#27)/// A `Service` is a function of a `Request`. It immediately returns a
[28](https://docs.rs#28)/// `Future` representing the eventual completion of processing the
[29](https://docs.rs#29)/// request. The actual request processing may happen at any time in the
[30](https://docs.rs#30)/// future, on any thread or executor. The processing may depend on calling
[31](https://docs.rs#31)/// other services. At some point in the future, the processing will complete,
[32](https://docs.rs#32)/// and the `Future` will resolve to a response or error.
[33](https://docs.rs#33)///
[34](https://docs.rs#34)/// At a high level, the `Service::call` function represents an RPC request. The
[35](https://docs.rs#35)/// `Service` value can be a server or a client.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)///
[37](https://docs.rs#37)/// # Server
[38](https://docs.rs#38)///
[39](https://docs.rs#39)/// An RPC server *implements* the `Service` trait. Requests received by the
[40](https://docs.rs#40)/// server over the network are deserialized and then passed as an argument to the
[41](https://docs.rs#41)/// server value. The returned response is sent back over the network.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)///
[43](https://docs.rs#43)/// As an example, here is how an HTTP request is processed by a server:
[44](https://docs.rs#44)///
[45](https://docs.rs#45)/// ```rust
[46](https://docs.rs#46)/// # use std::pin::Pin;
[47](https://docs.rs#47)/// # use std::task::{Poll, Context};
[48](https://docs.rs#48)/// # use std::future::Future;
[49](https://docs.rs#49)/// # use tower_service::Service;
[50](https://docs.rs#50)/// use http::{Request, Response, StatusCode};
[51](https://docs.rs#51)///
[52](https://docs.rs#52)/// struct HelloWorld;
[53](https://docs.rs#53)///
[54](https://docs.rs#54)/// impl Service<Request<Vec<u8>>> for HelloWorld {
[55](https://docs.rs#55)///     type Response = Response<Vec<u8>>;
[56](https://docs.rs#56)///     type Error = http::Error;
[57](https://docs.rs#57)///     type Future = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>>>>;
[58](https://docs.rs#58)///
[59](https://docs.rs#59)///     fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[60](https://docs.rs#60)///         Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
[61](https://docs.rs#61)///     }
[62](https://docs.rs#62)///
[63](https://docs.rs#63)///     fn call(&mut self, req: Request<Vec<u8>>) -> Self::Future {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)///         // create the body
[65](https://docs.rs#65)///         let body: Vec<u8> = "hello, world!\n"
[66](https://docs.rs#66)///             .as_bytes()
[67](https://docs.rs#67)///             .to_owned();
[68](https://docs.rs#68)///         // Create the HTTP response
[69](https://docs.rs#69)///         let resp = Response::builder()
[70](https://docs.rs#70)///             .status(StatusCode::OK)
[71](https://docs.rs#71)///             .body(body)
[72](https://docs.rs#72)///             .expect("Unable to create `http::Response`");
[73](https://docs.rs#73)///
[74](https://docs.rs#74)///         // create a response in a future.
[75](https://docs.rs#75)///         let fut = async {
[76](https://docs.rs#76)///             Ok(resp)
[77](https://docs.rs#77)///         };
[78](https://docs.rs#78)///
[79](https://docs.rs#79)///         // Return the response as an immediate future
[80](https://docs.rs#80)///         Box::pin(fut)
[81](https://docs.rs#81)///     }
[82](https://docs.rs#82)/// }
[83](https://docs.rs#83)/// ```
[84](https://docs.rs#84)///
[85](https://docs.rs#85)/// # Client
[86](https://docs.rs#86)///
[87](https://docs.rs#87)/// A client consumes a service by using a `Service` value. The client may
[88](https://docs.rs#88)/// issue requests by invoking `call` and passing the request as an argument.
[89](https://docs.rs#89)/// It then receives the response by waiting for the returned future.
[90](https://docs.rs#90)///
[91](https://docs.rs#91)/// As an example, here is how a Redis request would be issued:
[92](https://docs.rs#92)///
[93](https://docs.rs#93)/// ```rust,ignore
[94](https://docs.rs#94)/// let client = redis::Client::new()
[95](https://docs.rs#95)///     .connect("127.0.0.1:6379".parse().unwrap())
[96](https://docs.rs#96)///     .unwrap();
[97](https://docs.rs#97)///
[98](https://docs.rs#98)/// let resp = client.call(Cmd::set("foo", "this is the value of foo")).await?;
[99](https://docs.rs#99)///
[100](https://docs.rs#100)/// // Wait for the future to resolve
[101](https://docs.rs#101)/// println!("Redis response: {:?}", resp);
[102](https://docs.rs#102)/// ```
[103](https://docs.rs#103)///
[104](https://docs.rs#104)/// # Middleware / Layer
[105](https://docs.rs#105)///
[106](https://docs.rs#106)/// More often than not, all the pieces needed for writing robust, scalable
[107](https://docs.rs#107)/// network applications are the same no matter the underlying protocol. By
[108](https://docs.rs#108)/// unifying the API for both clients and servers in a protocol agnostic way,
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// it is possible to write middleware that provide these pieces in a
[110](https://docs.rs#110)/// reusable way.
[111](https://docs.rs#111)///
[112](https://docs.rs#112)/// Take timeouts as an example:
[113](https://docs.rs#113)///
[114](https://docs.rs#114)/// ```rust
[115](https://docs.rs#115)/// use tower_service::Service;
[116](https://docs.rs#116)/// use tower_layer::Layer;
[117](https://docs.rs#117)/// use futures::FutureExt;
[118](https://docs.rs#118)/// use std::future::Future;
[119](https://docs.rs#119)/// use std::task::{Context, Poll};
[120](https://docs.rs#120)/// use std::time::Duration;
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// use std::pin::Pin;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)/// use std::fmt;
[123](https://docs.rs#123)/// use std::error::Error;
[124](https://docs.rs#124)///
[125](https://docs.rs#125)/// // Our timeout service, which wraps another service and
[126](https://docs.rs#126)/// // adds a timeout to its response future.
[127](https://docs.rs#127)/// pub struct Timeout<T> {
[128](https://docs.rs#128)///     inner: T,
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///     timeout: Duration,
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// }
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// impl<T> Timeout<T> {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///     pub const fn new(inner: T, timeout: Duration) -> Timeout<T> {
[134](https://docs.rs#134)///         Timeout {
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///             inner,
[136](https://docs.rs#136)///             timeout
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///         }
[138](https://docs.rs#138)///     }
[139](https://docs.rs#139)/// }
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// // The error returned if processing a request timed out
[142](https://docs.rs#142)/// #[derive(Debug)]
[143](https://docs.rs#143)/// pub struct Expired;
[144](https://docs.rs#144)///
[145](https://docs.rs#145)/// impl fmt::Display for Expired {
[146](https://docs.rs#146)///     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[147](https://docs.rs#147)///         write!(f, "expired")
[148](https://docs.rs#148)///     }
[149](https://docs.rs#149)/// }
[150](https://docs.rs#150)///
[151](https://docs.rs#151)/// impl Error for Expired {}
[152](https://docs.rs#152)///
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// // We can implement `Service` for `Timeout<T>` if `T` is a `Service`
[154](https://docs.rs#154)/// impl<T, Request> Service<Request> for Timeout<T>
[155](https://docs.rs#155)/// where
[156](https://docs.rs#156)///     T: Service<Request>,
[157](https://docs.rs#157)///     T::Future: 'static,
[158](https://docs.rs#158)///     T::Error: Into<Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> + 'static,
[159](https://docs.rs#159)///     T::Response: 'static,
[160](https://docs.rs#160)/// {
[161](https://docs.rs#161)///     // `Timeout` doesn't modify the response type, so we use `T`'s response type
[162](https://docs.rs#162)///     type Response = T::Response;
[163](https://docs.rs#163)///     // Errors may be either `Expired` if the timeout expired, or the inner service's
[164](https://docs.rs#164)///     // `Error` type. Therefore, we return a boxed `dyn Error + Send + Sync` trait object to erase
[165](https://docs.rs#165)///     // the error's type.
[166](https://docs.rs#166)///     type Error = Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>;
[167](https://docs.rs#167)///     type Future = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>>>>;
[168](https://docs.rs#168)///
[169](https://docs.rs#169)///     fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[170](https://docs.rs#170)///         // Our timeout service is ready if the inner service is ready.
[171](https://docs.rs#171)///         // This is how backpressure can be propagated through a tree of nested services.
[172](https://docs.rs#172)///        self.inner.poll_ready(cx).map_err(Into::into)
[173](https://docs.rs#173)///     }
[174](https://docs.rs#174)///
[175](https://docs.rs#175)///     fn call(&mut self, req: Request) -> Self::Future {
[176](https://docs.rs#176)///         // Create a future that completes after `self.timeout`
[177](https://docs.rs#177)///         let timeout = tokio::time::sleep(self.timeout);
[178](https://docs.rs#178)///
[179](https://docs.rs#179)///         // Call the inner service and get a future that resolves to the response
[180](https://docs.rs#180)///         let fut = self.inner.call(req);
[181](https://docs.rs#181)///
[182](https://docs.rs#182)///         // Wrap those two futures in another future that completes when either one completes
[183](https://docs.rs#183)///         //
[184](https://docs.rs#184)///         // If the inner service is too slow the `sleep` future will complete first
[185](https://docs.rs#185)///         // And an error will be returned and `fut` will be dropped and not polled again
[186](https://docs.rs#186)///         //
[187](https://docs.rs#187)///         // We have to box the errors so the types match
[188](https://docs.rs#188)///         let f = async move {
[189](https://docs.rs#189)///             tokio::select! {
[190](https://docs.rs#190)///                 res = fut => {
[191](https://docs.rs#191)///                     res.map_err(|err| err.into())
[192](https://docs.rs#192)///                 },
[193](https://docs.rs#193)///                 _ = timeout => {
[194](https://docs.rs#194)///                     Err(Box::new(Expired) as Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)///                 },
[196](https://docs.rs#196)///             }
[197](https://docs.rs#197)///         };
[198](https://docs.rs#198)///
[199](https://docs.rs#199)///         Box::pin(f)
[200](https://docs.rs#200)///     }
[201](https://docs.rs#201)/// }
[202](https://docs.rs#202)///
[203](https://docs.rs#203)/// // A layer for wrapping services in `Timeout`
[204](https://docs.rs#204)/// pub struct TimeoutLayer(Duration);
[205](https://docs.rs#205)///
[206](https://docs.rs#206)/// impl TimeoutLayer {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)///     pub const fn new(delay: Duration) -> Self {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)///         TimeoutLayer(delay)
[209](https://docs.rs#209)///     }
[210](https://docs.rs#210)/// }
[211](https://docs.rs#211)///
[212](https://docs.rs#212)/// impl<S> Layer<S> for TimeoutLayer {
[213](https://docs.rs#213)///     type Service = Timeout<S>;
[214](https://docs.rs#214)///
[215](https://docs.rs#215)///     fn layer(&self, service: S) -> Timeout<S> {
[216](https://docs.rs#216)///         Timeout::new(service, self.0)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)///     }
[218](https://docs.rs#218)/// }
[219](https://docs.rs#219)/// ```
[220](https://docs.rs#220)///
[221](https://docs.rs#221)/// The above timeout implementation is decoupled from the underlying protocol
[222](https://docs.rs#222)/// and is also decoupled from client or server concerns. In other words, the
[223](https://docs.rs#223)/// same timeout middleware could be used in either a client or a server.
[224](https://docs.rs#224)///
[225](https://docs.rs#225)/// # Backpressure
[226](https://docs.rs#226)///
[227](https://docs.rs#227)/// Calling a `Service` which is at capacity (i.e., it is temporarily unable to process a
[228](https://docs.rs#228)/// request) should result in an error. The caller is responsible for ensuring
[229](https://docs.rs#229)/// that the service is ready to receive the request before calling it.
[230](https://docs.rs#230)///
[231](https://docs.rs#231)/// `Service` provides a mechanism by which the caller is able to coordinate
[232](https://docs.rs#232)/// readiness. `Service::poll_ready` returns `Ready` if the service expects that
[233](https://docs.rs#233)/// it is able to process a request.
[234](https://docs.rs#234)///
[235](https://docs.rs#235)/// # Be careful when cloning inner services
[236](https://docs.rs#236)///
[237](https://docs.rs#237)/// Services are permitted to panic if `call` is invoked without obtaining `Poll::Ready(Ok(()))`
[238](https://docs.rs#238)/// from `poll_ready`. You should therefore be careful when cloning services for example to move
[239](https://docs.rs#239)/// them into boxed futures. Even though the original service is ready, the clone might not be.
[240](https://docs.rs#240)///
[241](https://docs.rs#241)/// Therefore this kind of code is wrong and might panic:
[242](https://docs.rs#242)///
[243](https://docs.rs#243)/// ```rust
[244](https://docs.rs#244)/// # use std::pin::Pin;
[245](https://docs.rs#245)/// # use std::task::{Poll, Context};
[246](https://docs.rs#246)/// # use std::future::Future;
[247](https://docs.rs#247)/// # use tower_service::Service;
[248](https://docs.rs#248)/// #
[249](https://docs.rs#249)/// struct Wrapper<S> {
[250](https://docs.rs#250)///     inner: S,
[251](https://docs.rs#251)/// }
[252](https://docs.rs#252)///
[253](https://docs.rs#253)/// impl<R, S> Service<R> for Wrapper<S>
[254](https://docs.rs#254)/// where
[255](https://docs.rs#255)///     S: Service<R> + Clone + 'static,
[256](https://docs.rs#256)///     R: 'static,
[257](https://docs.rs#257)/// {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)///     type Response = S::Response;
[259](https://docs.rs#259)///     type Error = S::Error;
[260](https://docs.rs#260)///     type Future = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>>>>;
[261](https://docs.rs#261)///
[262](https://docs.rs#262)///     fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)///         self.inner.poll_ready(cx)
[264](https://docs.rs#264)///     }
[265](https://docs.rs#265)///
[266](https://docs.rs#266)///     fn call(&mut self, req: R) -> Self::Future {
[267](https://docs.rs#267)///         let mut inner = self.inner.clone();
[268](https://docs.rs#268)///         Box::pin(async move {
[269](https://docs.rs#269)///             // `inner` might not be ready since its a clone
[270](https://docs.rs#270)///             inner.call(req).await
[271](https://docs.rs#271)///         })
[272](https://docs.rs#272)///     }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)/// }
[274](https://docs.rs#274)/// ```
[275](https://docs.rs#275)///
[276](https://docs.rs#276)/// You should instead use [`std::mem::replace`] to take the service that was ready:
[277](https://docs.rs#277)///
[278](https://docs.rs#278)/// ```rust
[279](https://docs.rs#279)/// # use std::pin::Pin;
[280](https://docs.rs#280)/// # use std::task::{Poll, Context};
[281](https://docs.rs#281)/// # use std::future::Future;
[282](https://docs.rs#282)/// # use tower_service::Service;
[283](https://docs.rs#283)/// #
[284](https://docs.rs#284)/// struct Wrapper<S> {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)///     inner: S,
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)///
[288](https://docs.rs#288)/// impl<R, S> Service<R> for Wrapper<S>
[289](https://docs.rs#289)/// where
[290](https://docs.rs#290)///     S: Service<R> + Clone + 'static,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)///     R: 'static,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// {
[293](https://docs.rs#293)///     type Response = S::Response;
[294](https://docs.rs#294)///     type Error = S::Error;
[295](https://docs.rs#295)///     type Future = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>>>>;
[296](https://docs.rs#296)///
[297](https://docs.rs#297)///     fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)///         self.inner.poll_ready(cx)
[299](https://docs.rs#299)///     }
[300](https://docs.rs#300)///
[301](https://docs.rs#301)///     fn call(&mut self, req: R) -> Self::Future {
[302](https://docs.rs#302)///         let clone = self.inner.clone();
[303](https://docs.rs#303)///         // take the service that was ready
[304](https://docs.rs#304)///         let mut inner = std::mem::replace(&mut self.inner, clone);
[305](https://docs.rs#305)///         Box::pin(async move {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)///             inner.call(req).await
[307](https://docs.rs#307)///         })
[308](https://docs.rs#308)///     }
[309](https://docs.rs#309)/// }
[310](https://docs.rs#310)/// ```
[311](https://docs.rs#311)pub trait Service<Request> {
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    /// Responses given by the service.
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    type Response;
[314](https://docs.rs#314)
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    /// Errors produced by the service.
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    type Error;
[317](https://docs.rs#317)
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    /// The future response value.
[319](https://docs.rs#319)    type Future: Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>>;
[320](https://docs.rs#320)
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    /// Returns `Poll::Ready(Ok(()))` when the service is able to process requests.
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    ///
[323](https://docs.rs#323)    /// If the service is at capacity, then `Poll::Pending` is returned and the task
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    /// is notified when the service becomes ready again. This function is
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    /// expected to be called while on a task. Generally, this can be done with
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// a simple `futures::future::poll_fn` call.
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    ///
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    /// If `Poll::Ready(Err(_))` is returned, the service is no longer able to service requests
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    /// and the caller should discard the service instance.
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    ///
[331](https://docs.rs#331)    /// Once `poll_ready` returns `Poll::Ready(Ok(()))`, a request may be dispatched to the
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    /// service using `call`. Until a request is dispatched, repeated calls to
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    /// `poll_ready` must return either `Poll::Ready(Ok(()))` or `Poll::Ready(Err(_))`.
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    ///
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    /// Note that `poll_ready` may reserve shared resources that are consumed in a subsequent
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    /// invocation of `call`. Thus, it is critical for implementations to not assume that `call`
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    /// will always be invoked and to ensure that such resources are released if the service is
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    /// dropped before `call` is invoked or the future returned by `call` is dropped before it
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    /// is polled.
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>>;
[341](https://docs.rs#341)
[342](https://docs.rs#342)    /// Process the request and return the response asynchronously.
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    ///
[344](https://docs.rs#344)    /// This function is expected to be callable off task. As such,
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    /// implementations should take care to not call `poll_ready`.
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    ///
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    /// Before dispatching a request, `poll_ready` must be called and return
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    /// `Poll::Ready(Ok(()))`.
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    ///
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    /// # Panics
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    ///
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// Implementations are permitted to panic if `call` is invoked without
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    /// obtaining `Poll::Ready(Ok(()))` from `poll_ready`.
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    #[must_use = "futures do nothing unless you `.await` or poll them"]
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    fn call(&mut self, req: Request) -> Self::Future;
[356](https://docs.rs#356)}
[357](https://docs.rs#357)
[358](https://docs.rs#358)impl<'a, S, Request> Service<Request> for &'a mut S
[359](https://docs.rs#359)where
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    S: Service<Request> + 'a,
[361](https://docs.rs#361){
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    type Response = S::Response;
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    type Error = S::Error;
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    type Future = S::Future;
[365](https://docs.rs#365)
[366](https://docs.rs#366)    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), S::Error>> {
[367](https://docs.rs#367)        (**self).poll_ready(cx)
[368](https://docs.rs#368)    }
[369](https://docs.rs#369)
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    fn call(&mut self, request: Request) -> S::Future {
[371](https://docs.rs#371)        (**self).call(request)
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    }
[373](https://docs.rs#373)}
[374](https://docs.rs#374)
[375](https://docs.rs#375)impl<S, Request> Service<Request> for Box<S>
[376](https://docs.rs#376)where
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    S: Service<Request> + ?Sized,
[378](https://docs.rs#378){
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    type Response = S::Response;
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    type Error = S::Error;
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    type Future = S::Future;
[382](https://docs.rs#382)
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), S::Error>> {
[384](https://docs.rs#384)        (**self).poll_ready(cx)
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    }
[386](https://docs.rs#386)
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    fn call(&mut self, request: Request) -> S::Future {
[388](https://docs.rs#388)        (**self).call(request)
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    }
[390](https://docs.rs#390)}

# Either in tower::util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower/*/tower/util/enum.Either.html

```
pub enum Either<A, B> {
    Left(A),
    Right(B),
}
```
Available on

**crate feature**only.`util`## Expand description

Combine two different service types into a single type.

Both services must be of the same request, response, and error types.
[ Either](https://docs.rs/enum.Either.html) is useful for handling conditional branching in service middleware
to different inner service types.

[102](#102)    fn update_pending_from_discover(
[106](#106)        &mut self,
[107](#107)        cx: &mut Context<'_>,
[108](#108)    ) -> Poll<Option<Result<(), error::Discover>>> {
[109](#109)        debug!("updating from discover");
[110](#110)        loop {
[111](#111)            match ready!(Pin::new(&mut self.discover).poll_discover(cx))
[112](#112)                .transpose()
[113](#113)                .map_err(|e| error::Discover(e.into()))?
[114](#114)            {
[115](#115)                None => return Poll::Ready(None),
[116](#116)                Some(Change::Remove(key)) => {
[117](#117)                    trace!("remove");
[118](#118)                    self.services.evict(&key);
[119](#119)                }
[120](#120)                Some(Change::Insert(key, svc)) => {
[121](#121)                    trace!("insert");
[122](#122)                    self.services.push(key, svc);
[125](#125)                }
[126](#126)            }
[127](#127)        }
[128](#128)    }
[129](#129)
[130](#130)    fn promote_pending_to_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) {
[131](#131)        loop {
[132](#132)            match self.services.poll_pending(cx) {
[133](#133)                Poll::Ready(Ok(())) => {
[134](#134)                    debug_assert_eq!(self.services.pending_len(), 0);
[136](#136)                    break;
[137](#137)                }
[138](#138)                Poll::Pending => {
[139](#139)                    debug_assert!(self.services.pending_len() > 0);
[141](#141)                    break;
[142](#142)                }
[143](#143)                Poll::Ready(Err(error)) => {
[144](#144)                    debug!(%error, "dropping failed endpoint");
[147](#147)                }
[148](#148)            }
[149](#149)        }
[150](#150)        trace!(
[151](#151)            ready = %self.services.ready_len(),
[152](#152)            pending = %self.services.pending_len(),
[153](#153)            "poll_unready"
[154](#154)        );
[155](#155)    }
[156](#156)
[157](#157)    fn p2c_ready_index(&mut self) -> Option<usize> {
[159](#159)        match self.services.ready_len() {
[160](#160)            0 => None,
[161](#161)            1 => Some(0),
[162](#162)            len => {
[163](#163)                let [aidx, bidx] = sample_floyd2(&mut self.rng, len as u64);
[166](#166)                debug_assert_ne!(aidx, bidx, "random indices must be distinct");
[167](#167)
[168](#168)                let aload = self.ready_index_load(aidx as usize);
[169](#169)                let bload = self.ready_index_load(bidx as usize);
[170](#170)                let chosen = if aload <= bload { aidx } else { bidx };
[171](#171)
[172](#172)                trace!(
[173](#173)                    a.index = aidx,
[174](#174)                    a.load = ?aload,
[175](#175)                    b.index = bidx,
[176](#176)                    b.load = ?bload,
[177](#177)                    chosen = if chosen == aidx { "a" } else { "b" },
[178](#178)                    "p2c",
[179](#179)                );
[180](#180)                Some(chosen as usize)
[181](#181)            }

`discover`## Expand description

A dynamically changing set of related services.

As new services arrive and old services are retired,
[ Change](https://docs.rs/enum.Change.html)s are returned which provide unique identifiers
for the services.

See the module documentation for more details.

[9](https://docs.rs#9)/// Returns a new [`FutureService`] for the given future.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)///
[11](https://docs.rs#11)/// A [`FutureService`] allows you to treat a future that resolves to a service as a service. This
[12](https://docs.rs#12)/// can be useful for services that are created asynchronously.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)///
[14](https://docs.rs#14)/// # Example
[15](https://docs.rs#15)/// ```
[16](https://docs.rs#16)/// use tower::{service_fn, Service, ServiceExt};
[17](https://docs.rs#17)/// use tower::util::future_service;
[18](https://docs.rs#18)/// use std::convert::Infallible;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)///
[20](https://docs.rs#20)/// # fn main() {
[21](https://docs.rs#21)/// # async {
[22](https://docs.rs#22)/// // A future which outputs a type implementing `Service`.
[23](https://docs.rs#23)/// let future_of_a_service = async {
[24](https://docs.rs#24)///     let svc = service_fn(|_req: ()| async { Ok::<_, Infallible>("ok") });
[25](https://docs.rs#25)///     Ok::<_, Infallible>(svc)
[26](https://docs.rs#26)/// };
[27](https://docs.rs#27)///
[28](https://docs.rs#28)/// // Wrap the future with a `FutureService`, allowing it to be used
[29](https://docs.rs#29)/// // as a service without awaiting the future's completion:
[30](https://docs.rs#30)/// let mut svc = future_service(Box::pin(future_of_a_service));
[31](https://docs.rs#31)///
[32](https://docs.rs#32)/// // Now, when we wait for the service to become ready, it will
[33](https://docs.rs#33)/// // drive the future to completion internally.
[34](https://docs.rs#34)/// let svc = svc.ready().await.unwrap();
[35](https://docs.rs#35)/// let res = svc.call(()).await.unwrap();
[36](https://docs.rs#36)/// # };
[37](https://docs.rs#37)/// # }
[38](https://docs.rs#38)/// ```
[39](https://docs.rs#39)///
[40](https://docs.rs#40)/// # Regarding the [`Unpin`] bound
[41](https://docs.rs#41)///
[42](https://docs.rs#42)/// The [`Unpin`] bound on `F` is necessary because the future will be polled in
[43](https://docs.rs#43)/// [`Service::poll_ready`] which doesn't have a pinned receiver (it takes `&mut self` and not `self:
[44](https://docs.rs#44)/// Pin<&mut Self>`). So we cannot put the future into a `Pin` without requiring `Unpin`.
[45](https://docs.rs#45)///
[46](https://docs.rs#46)/// This will most likely come up if you're calling `future_service` with an async block. In that
[47](https://docs.rs#47)/// case you can use `Box::pin(async { ... })` as shown in the example.

### impl<F, S> [FutureService](https://docs.rs/struct.FutureService.html)<F, S>

Returns a new [ FutureService](https://docs.rs/struct.FutureService.html) for the given future.

A [ FutureService](https://docs.rs/struct.FutureService.html) allows you to treat a future that resolves to a service as a service. This
can be useful for services that are created asynchronously.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use tower::{service_fn, Service, ServiceExt};
use tower::util::FutureService;
use std::convert::Infallible;
// A future which outputs a type implementing `Service`.
let future_of_a_service = async {
    let svc = service_fn(|_req: ()| async { Ok::<_, Infallible>("ok") });
    Ok::<_, Infallible>(svc)
};
// Wrap the future with a `FutureService`, allowing it to be used
// as a service without awaiting the future's completion:
let mut svc = FutureService::new(Box::pin(future_of_a_service));
// Now, when we wait for the service to become ready, it will
// drive the future to completion internally.
let svc = svc.ready().await.unwrap();
let res = svc.call(()).await.unwrap();
```
The [ Unpin](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Unpin.html) bound on

`F` is necessary because the future will be polled in
[which doesn’t have a pinned receiver (it takes](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html#tymethod.poll_ready)

`Service::poll_ready``&mut self` and not `self: Pin<&mut Self>`). So we cannot put the future into a `Pin` without requiring `Unpin`.This will most likely come up if you’re calling `future_service` with an async block. In that
case you can use `Box::pin(async { ... })` as shown in the example.

# tower/make/make_service.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Contains [`MakeService`] which is a trait alias for a [`Service`] of [`Service`]s.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)
[3](https://docs.rs#3)use crate::sealed::Sealed;
[4](https://docs.rs#4)use std::fmt;
[5](https://docs.rs#5)use std::future::Future;
[6](https://docs.rs#6)use std::marker::PhantomData;
[7](https://docs.rs#7)use std::task::{Context, Poll};
[8](https://docs.rs#8)use tower_service::Service;
[9](https://docs.rs#9)
[10](https://docs.rs#10)pub(crate) mod shared;
[11](https://docs.rs#11)
[12](https://docs.rs#12)/// Creates new [`Service`] values.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)///
[14](https://docs.rs#14)/// Acts as a service factory. This is useful for cases where new [`Service`]
[15](https://docs.rs#15)/// values must be produced. One case is a TCP server listener. The listener
[16](https://docs.rs#16)/// accepts new TCP streams, obtains a new [`Service`] value using the
[17](https://docs.rs#17)/// [`MakeService`] trait, and uses that new [`Service`] value to process inbound
[18](https://docs.rs#18)/// requests on that new TCP stream.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)///
[20](https://docs.rs#20)/// This is essentially a trait alias for a [`Service`] of [`Service`]s.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)pub trait MakeService<Target, Request>: Sealed<(Target, Request)> {
[22](https://docs.rs#22)    /// Responses given by the service
[23](https://docs.rs#23)    type Response;
[24](https://docs.rs#24)
[25](https://docs.rs#25)    /// Errors produced by the service
[26](https://docs.rs#26)    type Error;
[27](https://docs.rs#27)
[28](https://docs.rs#28)    /// The [`Service`] value created by this factory
[29](https://docs.rs#29)    type Service: Service<Request, Response = Self::Response, Error = Self::Error>;
[30](https://docs.rs#30)
[31](https://docs.rs#31)    /// Errors produced while building a service.
[32](https://docs.rs#32)    type MakeError;
[33](https://docs.rs#33)
[34](https://docs.rs#34)    /// The future of the [`Service`] instance.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)    type Future: Future<Output = Result<Self::Service, Self::MakeError>>;
[36](https://docs.rs#36)
[37](https://docs.rs#37)    /// Returns [`Poll::Ready`] when the factory is able to create more services.
[38](https://docs.rs#38)    ///
[39](https://docs.rs#39)    /// If the service is at capacity, then [`Poll::Pending`] is returned and the task
[40](https://docs.rs#40)    /// is notified when the service becomes ready again. This function is
[41](https://docs.rs#41)    /// expected to be called while on a task.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)    ///
[43](https://docs.rs#43)    /// [`Poll::Ready`]: std::task::Poll::Ready
[44](https://docs.rs#44)    /// [`Poll::Pending`]: std::task::Poll::Pending
[45](https://docs.rs#45)    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::MakeError>>;
[46](https://docs.rs#46)
[47](https://docs.rs#47)    /// Create and return a new service value asynchronously.
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    fn make_service(&mut self, target: Target) -> Self::Future;
[49](https://docs.rs#49)
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    /// Consume this [`MakeService`] and convert it into a [`Service`].
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    ///
[52](https://docs.rs#52)    /// # Example
[53](https://docs.rs#53)    /// ```
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    /// use std::convert::Infallible;
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    /// use tower::Service;
[56](https://docs.rs#56)    /// use tower::make::MakeService;
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    /// use tower::service_fn;
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    ///
[59](https://docs.rs#59)    /// # fn main() {
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    /// # async {
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    /// // A `MakeService`
[62](https://docs.rs#62)    /// let make_service = service_fn(|make_req: ()| async {
[63](https://docs.rs#63)    ///     Ok::<_, Infallible>(service_fn(|req: String| async {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    ///         Ok::<_, Infallible>(req)
[65](https://docs.rs#65)    ///     }))
[66](https://docs.rs#66)    /// });
[67](https://docs.rs#67)    ///
[68](https://docs.rs#68)    /// // Convert the `MakeService` into a `Service`
[69](https://docs.rs#69)    /// let mut svc = make_service.into_service();
[70](https://docs.rs#70)    ///
[71](https://docs.rs#71)    /// // Make a new service
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    /// let mut new_svc = svc.call(()).await.unwrap();
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    ///
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    /// // Call the service
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    /// let res = new_svc.call("foo".to_string()).await.unwrap();
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// # };
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    /// # }
[78](https://docs.rs#78)    /// ```
[79](https://docs.rs#79)    fn into_service(self) -> IntoService<Self, Request>
[80](https://docs.rs#80)    where
[81](https://docs.rs#81)        Self: Sized,
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    {
[83](https://docs.rs#83)        IntoService {
[84](https://docs.rs#84)            make: self,
[85](https://docs.rs#85)            _marker: PhantomData,
[86](https://docs.rs#86)        }
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    }
[88](https://docs.rs#88)
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    /// Convert this [`MakeService`] into a [`Service`] without consuming the original [`MakeService`].
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    ///

[92](https://docs.rs#92)    /// ```

[84](#84)    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[85](#85)        loop {
[86](#86)            match &mut self.state {
[87](#87)                State::Idle => {
[88](#88)                    trace!("poll_ready; idle");
[89](#89)                    match self.mk_service.poll_ready(cx) {
[90](#90)                        Poll::Ready(r) => r?,
[91](#91)                        Poll::Pending => {
[92](#92)                            trace!("poll_ready; MakeService not ready");
[93](#93)                            return Poll::Pending;
[94](#94)                        }
[95](#95)                    }
[96](#96)
[97](#97)                    let fut = self.mk_service.make_service(self.target.clone());
[98](#98)                    self.state = State::Connecting(fut);
[99](#99)                    continue;
[100](#100)                }
[101](#101)                State::Connecting(ref mut f) => {
[102](#102)                    trace!("poll_ready; connecting");
[103](#103)                    match Pin::new(f).poll(cx) {
[104](#104)                        Poll::Ready(Ok(service)) => {
[105](#105)                            self.state = State::Connected(service);
[106](#106)                        }
[107](#107)                        Poll::Pending => {
[108](#108)                            trace!("poll_ready; not ready");
[109](#109)                            return Poll::Pending;
[110](#110)                        }
[111](#111)                        Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => {
[112](#112)                            trace!("poll_ready; error");
[113](#113)                            self.state = State::Idle;
[114](#114)                            self.error = Some(e);
[115](#115)                            break;
[116](#116)                        }
[117](#117)                    }
[118](#118)                }
[119](#119)                State::Connected(ref mut inner) => {
[120](#120)                    trace!("poll_ready; connected");
[121](#121)                    match inner.poll_ready(cx) {
[122](#122)                        Poll::Ready(Ok(())) => {
[123](#123)                            trace!("poll_ready; ready");
[124](#124)                            return Poll::Ready(Ok(()));
[125](#125)                        }
[126](#126)                        Poll::Pending => {
[127](#127)                            trace!("poll_ready; not ready");
[128](#128)                            return Poll::Pending;
[129](#129)                        }
[130](#130)                        Poll::Ready(Err(_)) => {
[131](#131)                            trace!("poll_ready; error");
[132](#132)                            self.state = State::Idle;
[133](#133)                        }
[134](#134)                    }
[135](#135)                }
[136](#136)            }
[137](#137)        }
[138](#138)
[139](#139)        Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
[140](#140)    }

[143](#143)        if let Some(error) = self.error.take() {
[144](#144)            return ResponseFuture::error(error);

[148](#148)            State::Connected(ref mut service) => service,

# Policy in tower::retry - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower/*/tower/retry/trait.Policy.html

```
pub trait Policy<Req, Res, E> {
    type
```
[Future](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Future): [Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>;
    // Required methods
    fn [retry](https://docs.rs#tymethod.retry)(
        &mut self,
        req: [&mut Req](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
        result: &mut [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Res, E>,
    ) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self::[Future](https://docs.rs/trait.Policy.html#associatedtype.Future)>;
[clone_request](https://docs.rs#tymethod.clone_request)(&mut self, req: [&Req](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Req>;
}**crate feature**only.

`retry`## Expand description

A “retry policy” to classify if a request should be retried.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use tower::retry::Policy;
use std::future;
type Req = String;
type Res = String;
struct Attempts(usize);
impl<E> Policy<Req, Res, E> for Attempts {
    type Future = future::Ready<()>;
    fn retry(&mut self, req: &mut Req, result: &mut Result<Res, E>) -> Option<Self::Future> {
        match result {
            Ok(_) => {
                // Treat all `Response`s as success,
                // so don't retry...
                None
            },
            Err(_) => {
                // Treat all errors as failures...
                // But we limit the number of attempts...
                if self.0 > 0 {
                    // Try again!
                    self.0 -= 1;
                    Some(future::ready(()))
                } else {
                    // Used all our attempts, no retry...
                    None
                }
            }
        }
    }
    fn clone_request(&mut self, req: &Req) -> Option<Req> {
        Some(req.clone())
    }
}
```
## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Check the policy if a certain request should be retried.

This method is passed a reference to the original request, and either
the [ Service::Response](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html#associatedtype.Response) or

[from the inner service.](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html#associatedtype.Error)

`Service::Error`If the request should **not** be retried, return `None`.

If the request *should* be retried, return `Some` future that will delay
the next retry of the request. This can be used to sleep for a certain
duration, to wait for some external condition to be met before retrying,
or resolve right away, if the request should be retried immediately.

[§](https://docs.rs#mutating-requests)Mutating Requests

The policy MAY chose to mutate the `req`: if the request is mutated, the
mutated request will be sent to the inner service in the next retry.
This can be helpful for use cases like tracking the retry count in a
header.

[§](https://docs.rs#mutating-results)Mutating Results

The policy MAY chose to mutate the result. This enables the retry policy to convert a failure into a success and vice versa. For example, if the policy is used to poll while waiting for a state change, the policy can switch the result to emit a specific error when retries are exhausted.

The policy can also record metadata on the request to include information about the number of retries required or to record that a failure failed after exhausting all retries.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

[28](https://docs.rs#28)    /// Creates a new [`Buffer`] wrapping `service`.
[29](https://docs.rs#29)    ///
[30](https://docs.rs#30)    /// `bound` gives the maximal number of requests that can be queued for the service before
[31](https://docs.rs#31)    /// backpressure is applied to callers.
[32](https://docs.rs#32)    ///
[33](https://docs.rs#33)    /// The default Tokio executor is used to run the given service, which means that this method
[34](https://docs.rs#34)    /// must be called while on the Tokio runtime.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)    ///
[36](https://docs.rs#36)    /// # A note on choosing a `bound`
[37](https://docs.rs#37)    ///
[38](https://docs.rs#38)    /// When [`Buffer`]'s implementation of [`poll_ready`] returns [`Poll::Ready`], it reserves a
[39](https://docs.rs#39)    /// slot in the channel for the forthcoming [`call`]. However, if this call doesn't arrive,
[40](https://docs.rs#40)    /// this reserved slot may be held up for a long time. As a result, it's advisable to set
[41](https://docs.rs#41)    /// `bound` to be at least the maximum number of concurrent requests the [`Buffer`] will see.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)    /// If you do not, all the slots in the buffer may be held up by futures that have just called
[43](https://docs.rs#43)    /// [`poll_ready`] but will not issue a [`call`], which prevents other senders from issuing new
[44](https://docs.rs#44)    /// requests.
[45](https://docs.rs#45)    ///
[46](https://docs.rs#46)    /// [`Poll::Ready`]: std::task::Poll::Ready
[47](https://docs.rs#47)    /// [`call`]: crate::Service::call
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    /// [`poll_ready`]: crate::Service::poll_ready
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    pub fn new<S>(service: S, bound: usize) -> Self
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    where
[51](https://docs.rs#51)        S: Service<Req, Future = F> + Send + 'static,
[52](https://docs.rs#52)        F: Send,
[53](https://docs.rs#53)        S::Error: Into<crate::BoxError> + Send + Sync,
[54](https://docs.rs#54)        Req: Send + 'static,
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    {
[56](https://docs.rs#56)        let (service, worker) = Self::pair(service, bound);
[57](https://docs.rs#57)        tokio::spawn(worker);
[58](https://docs.rs#58)        service
[59](https://docs.rs#59)    }
[60](https://docs.rs#60)
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    /// Creates a new [`Buffer`] wrapping `service`, but returns the background worker.
[62](https://docs.rs#62)    ///
[63](https://docs.rs#63)    /// This is useful if you do not want to spawn directly onto the tokio runtime
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    /// but instead want to use your own executor. This will return the [`Buffer`] and
[65](https://docs.rs#65)    /// the background `Worker` that you can then spawn.
[66](https://docs.rs#66)    pub fn pair<S>(service: S, bound: usize) -> (Self, Worker<S, Req>)
[67](https://docs.rs#67)    where
[68](https://docs.rs#68)        S: Service<Req, Future = F> + Send + 'static,

[97](https://docs.rs#97)    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[98](https://docs.rs#98)        // First, check if the worker is still alive.
[99](https://docs.rs#99)        if self.tx.is_closed() {
[100](https://docs.rs#100)            // If the inner service has errored, then we error here.
[101](https://docs.rs#101)            return Poll::Ready(Err(self.get_worker_error()));
[102](https://docs.rs#102)        }
[103](https://docs.rs#103)
[104](https://docs.rs#104)        // Poll the sender to acquire a permit.
[105](https://docs.rs#105)        self.tx
[106](https://docs.rs#106)            .poll_reserve(cx)
[107](https://docs.rs#107)            .map_err(|_| self.get_worker_error())
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    }
[109](https://docs.rs#109)
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    fn call(&mut self, request: Req) -> Self::Future {
[111](https://docs.rs#111)        tracing::trace!("sending request to buffer worker");
[112](https://docs.rs#112)
[113](https://docs.rs#113)        // get the current Span so that we can explicitly propagate it to the worker
[114](https://docs.rs#114)        // if we didn't do this, events on the worker related to this span wouldn't be counted
[115](https://docs.rs#115)        // towards that span since the worker would have no way of entering it.
[116](https://docs.rs#116)        let span = tracing::Span::current();
[117](https://docs.rs#117)
[118](https://docs.rs#118)        // If we've made it here, then a channel permit has already been
[119](https://docs.rs#119)        // acquired, so we can freely allocate a oneshot.
[120](https://docs.rs#120)        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
[121](https://docs.rs#121)
[122](https://docs.rs#122)        match self.tx.send_item(Message { request, span, tx }) {
[123](https://docs.rs#123)            Ok(_) => ResponseFuture::new(rx),
[124](https://docs.rs#124)            // If the channel is closed, propagate the error from the worker.
[125](https://docs.rs#125)            Err(_) => {
[126](https://docs.rs#126)                tracing::trace!("buffer channel closed");
[127](https://docs.rs#127)                ResponseFuture::failed(self.get_worker_error())
[128](https://docs.rs#128)            }
[129](https://docs.rs#129)        }
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    }
[131](https://docs.rs#131)}

[216](#216)impl RttEstimate {
[219](#219)    fn new(rtt_ns: f64) -> Self {
[220](#220)        debug_assert!(0.0 < rtt_ns, "rtt must be positive");
[221](#221)        Self {
[222](#222)            rtt_ns,
[223](#223)            update_at: Instant::now(),
[224](#224)        }
[225](#225)    }
[226](#226)
[227](#227)    fn decay(&mut self, decay_ns: f64) -> f64 {
[229](#229)        let now = Instant::now();
[231](#231)        self.update(now, now, decay_ns)
[232](#232)    }
[233](#233)
[234](#234)    fn update(&mut self, sent_at: Instant, recv_at: Instant, decay_ns: f64) -> f64 {
[238](#238)        debug_assert!(
[239](#239)            sent_at <= recv_at,
[240](#240)            "recv_at={:?} after sent_at={:?}",
[241](#241)            recv_at,
[242](#242)            sent_at
[243](#243)        );
[244](#244)        let rtt = nanos(recv_at.saturating_duration_since(sent_at));
[245](#245)
[246](#246)        let now = Instant::now();
[247](#247)        debug_assert!(
[248](#248)            self.update_at <= now,
[249](#249)            "update_at={:?} in the future",
[250](#250)            self.update_at
[251](#251)        );
[252](#252)
[253](#253)        self.rtt_ns = if self.rtt_ns < rtt {
[254](#254)            trace!(
[257](#257)                "update peak rtt={}ms prior={}ms",
[258](#258)                rtt / NANOS_PER_MILLI,
[259](#259)                self.rtt_ns / NANOS_PER_MILLI,
[260](#260)            );
[261](#261)            rtt
[262](#262)        } else {
[263](#263)            let elapsed = nanos(now.saturating_duration_since(self.update_at));
[268](#268)            let decay = (-elapsed / decay_ns).exp();
[269](#269)            let recency = 1.0 - decay;
[270](#270)            let next_estimate = (self.rtt_ns * decay) + (rtt * recency);
[271](#271)            trace!(
[272](#272)                "update rtt={:03.0}ms decay={:06.0}ns; next={:03.0}ms",
[273](#273)                rtt / NANOS_PER_MILLI,
[274](#274)                self.rtt_ns - next_estimate,
[275](#275)                next_estimate / NANOS_PER_MILLI,
[276](#276)            );
[277](#277)            next_estimate
[278](#278)        };
[279](#279)        self.update_at = now;
[280](#280)
[281](#281)        self.rtt_ns
[282](#282)    }
[283](#283)}

[293](#293)        }
[294](#294)    }

# TrackCompletion in tower::load::completion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower/*/tower/load/completion/trait.TrackCompletion.html

`pub trait TrackCompletion<H, V>: `[Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html) {
    type [Output](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Output);
    // Required method
    fn [track_completion](https://docs.rs#tymethod.track_completion)(&self, handle: H, value: V) -> Self::[Output](https://docs.rs/trait.TrackCompletion.html#associatedtype.Output);
}**crate feature**only.

`load`## Expand description

Attaches `H`-typed completion tracker to `V` typed values.

Handles (of type `H`) are intended to be RAII guards that primarily implement [ Drop](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html) and update
load metric state as they are dropped. This trait allows implementors to “forward” the handle
to later parts of the request-handling pipeline, so that the handle is only dropped when the
request has truly completed.

This utility allows load metrics to have a protocol-agnostic means to track streams past their
initial response future. For example, if `V` represents an HTTP response type, an
implementation could add `H`-typed handles to each response’s extensions to detect when all the
response’s extensions have been dropped.

A base `impl<H, V> TrackCompletion<H, V> for CompleteOnResponse` is provided to drop the handle
once the response future is resolved. This is appropriate when a response is discrete and
cannot comprise multiple messages.

In many cases, the `Output` type is simply `V`. However, [ TrackCompletion](https://docs.rs/trait.TrackCompletion.html) may alter the type
in order to instrument it appropriately. For example, an HTTP

[may modify the body type: so a](https://docs.rs/trait.TrackCompletion.html)

`TrackCompletion`[that takes values of type](https://docs.rs/trait.TrackCompletion.html)

`TrackCompletion`[may output values of type](https://docs.rs/http/latest/http/response/struct.Response.html)

`http::Response<A>`[.](https://docs.rs/http/latest/http/response/struct.Response.html)

`http::Response<B>`## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# Hedge in tower::hedge - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower/*/tower/hedge/struct.Hedge.html

`pub struct Hedge<S, P>(/* private fields */);`Available on

**crate feature**only.`hedge`## Expand description

A middleware that pre-emptively retries requests which have been outstanding for longer than a given latency percentile. If either of the original future or the retry future completes, that value is used.

# tower/steer/mod.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! This module provides functionality to aid managing routing requests between [`Service`]s.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! # Example
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! [`Steer`] can for example be used to create a router, akin to what you might find in web
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! frameworks.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! Here, `GET /` will be sent to the `root` service, while all other requests go to `not_found`.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! ```rust
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! # use std::task::{Context, Poll, ready};
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! # use tower_service::Service;
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! # use tower::steer::Steer;
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! # use tower::service_fn;
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! # use tower::util::BoxService;
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! # use tower::ServiceExt;
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! # use std::convert::Infallible;
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! use http::{Request, Response, StatusCode, Method};
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! # #[tokio::main]
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! # async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! // Service that responds to `GET /`
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! let root = service_fn(|req: Request<String>| async move {
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!     # assert_eq!(req.uri().path(), "/");
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!     let res = Response::new("Hello, World!".to_string());
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!     Ok::<_, Infallible>(res)
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! });
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! // We have to box the service so its type gets erased and we can put it in a `Vec` with other
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! // services
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! let root = BoxService::new(root);
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! // Service that responds with `404 Not Found` to all requests
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! let not_found = service_fn(|req: Request<String>| async move {
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!     let res = Response::builder()
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!         .status(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND)
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!         .body(String::new())
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!         .expect("response is valid");
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!     Ok::<_, Infallible>(res)
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! });
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! // Box that as well
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! let not_found = BoxService::new(not_found);
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! let mut svc = Steer::new(
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!     // All services we route between
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!     vec![root, not_found],
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     // How we pick which service to send the request to
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!     |req: &Request<String>, _services: &[_]| {
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!         if req.method() == Method::GET && req.uri().path() == "/" {
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!             0 // Index of `root`
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!         } else {
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!             1 // Index of `not_found`
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!         }
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!     },
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! );
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! // This request will get sent to `root`
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! let req = Request::get("/").body(String::new()).unwrap();
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! let res = svc.ready().await?.call(req).await?;
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! assert_eq!(res.into_body(), "Hello, World!");
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! // This request will get sent to `not_found`
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! let req = Request::get("/does/not/exist").body(String::new()).unwrap();
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! let res = svc.ready().await?.call(req).await?;
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! assert_eq!(res.into_body(), "");
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! #
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! # Ok(())
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! # }
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! ```
[70](https://docs.rs#70)use std::task::{Context, Poll};
[71](https://docs.rs#71)use std::{collections::VecDeque, fmt, marker::PhantomData};
[72](https://docs.rs#72)use tower_service::Service;
[73](https://docs.rs#73)
[74](https://docs.rs#74)/// This is how callers of [`Steer`] tell it which `Service` a `Req` corresponds to.
[75](https://docs.rs#75)pub trait Picker<S, Req> {
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// Return an index into the iterator of `Service` passed to [`Steer::new`].
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    fn pick(&mut self, r: &Req, services: &[S]) -> usize;
[78](https://docs.rs#78)}
[79](https://docs.rs#79)
[80](https://docs.rs#80)impl<S, F, Req> Picker<S, Req> for F
[81](https://docs.rs#81)where
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    F: Fn(&Req, &[S]) -> usize,
[83](https://docs.rs#83){
[84](https://docs.rs#84)    fn pick(&mut self, r: &Req, services: &[S]) -> usize {
[85](https://docs.rs#85)        self(r, services)
[86](https://docs.rs#86)    }
[87](https://docs.rs#87)}
[88](https://docs.rs#88)
[89](https://docs.rs#89)/// [`Steer`] manages a list of [`Service`]s which all handle the same type of request.
[90](https://docs.rs#90)///
[91](https://docs.rs#91)/// An example use case is a sharded service.
[92](https://docs.rs#92)/// It accepts new requests, then:
[93](https://docs.rs#93)/// 1. Determines, via the provided [`Picker`], which [`Service`] the request corresponds to.
[94](https://docs.rs#94)/// 2. Waits (in [`Service::poll_ready`]) for *all* services to be ready.
[95](https://docs.rs#95)/// 3. Calls the correct [`Service`] with the request, and returns a future corresponding to the
[96](https://docs.rs#96)///    call.
[97](https://docs.rs#97)///
[98](https://docs.rs#98)/// Note that [`Steer`] must wait for all services to be ready since it can't know ahead of time
[99](https://docs.rs#99)/// which [`Service`] the next message will arrive for, and is unwilling to buffer items
[100](https://docs.rs#100)/// indefinitely. This will cause head-of-line blocking unless paired with a [`Service`] that does
[101](https://docs.rs#101)/// buffer items indefinitely, and thus always returns [`Poll::Ready`]. For example, wrapping each
[102](https://docs.rs#102)/// component service with a [`Buffer`] with a high enough limit (the maximum number of concurrent
[103](https://docs.rs#103)/// requests) will prevent head-of-line blocking in [`Steer`].
[104](https://docs.rs#104)///
[105](https://docs.rs#105)/// [`Buffer`]: crate::buffer::Buffer
[106](https://docs.rs#106)pub struct Steer<S, F, Req> {
[107](https://docs.rs#107)    router: F,
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    services: Vec<S>,
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    not_ready: VecDeque<usize>,
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    _phantom: PhantomData<Req>,
[111](https://docs.rs#111)}
[112](https://docs.rs#112)
[113](https://docs.rs#113)impl<S, F, Req> Steer<S, F, Req> {
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    /// Make a new [`Steer`] with a list of [`Service`]'s and a [`Picker`].
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    ///
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// Note: the order of the [`Service`]'s is significant for [`Picker::pick`]'s return value.
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    pub fn new(services: impl IntoIterator<Item = S>, router: F) -> Self {
[118](https://docs.rs#118)        let services: Vec<_> = services.into_iter().collect();
[119](https://docs.rs#119)        let not_ready: VecDeque<_> = services.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, _)| i).collect();
[120](https://docs.rs#120)        Self {
[121](https://docs.rs#121)            router,
[122](https://docs.rs#122)            services,
[123](https://docs.rs#123)            not_ready,
[124](https://docs.rs#124)            _phantom: PhantomData,
[125](https://docs.rs#125)        }
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    }
[127](https://docs.rs#127)}
[128](https://docs.rs#128)
[129](https://docs.rs#129)impl<S, Req, F> Service<Req> for Steer<S, F, Req>
[130](https://docs.rs#130)where
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    S: Service<Req>,
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    F: Picker<S, Req>,
[133](https://docs.rs#133){
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    type Response = S::Response;
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    type Error = S::Error;
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    type Future = S::Future;
[137](https://docs.rs#137)
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[139](https://docs.rs#139)        loop {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)            // must wait for *all* services to be ready.
[141](https://docs.rs#141)            // this will cause head-of-line blocking unless the underlying services are always ready.
[142](https://docs.rs#142)            if self.not_ready.is_empty() {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)                return Poll::Ready(Ok(()));
[144](https://docs.rs#144)            } else {
[145](https://docs.rs#145)                if self.services[self.not_ready[0]]
[146](https://docs.rs#146)                    .poll_ready(cx)?
[147](https://docs.rs#147)                    .is_pending()
[148](https://docs.rs#148)                {
[149](https://docs.rs#149)                    return Poll::Pending;
[150](https://docs.rs#150)                }
[151](https://docs.rs#151)
[152](https://docs.rs#152)                self.not_ready.pop_front();
[153](https://docs.rs#153)            }
[154](https://docs.rs#154)        }
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    }
[156](https://docs.rs#156)
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    fn call(&mut self, req: Req) -> Self::Future {
[158](https://docs.rs#158)        assert!(
[159](https://docs.rs#159)            self.not_ready.is_empty(),
[160](https://docs.rs#160)            "Steer must wait for all services to be ready. Did you forget to call poll_ready()?"
[161](https://docs.rs#161)        );
[162](https://docs.rs#162)
[163](https://docs.rs#163)        let idx = self.router.pick(&req, &self.services[..]);
[164](https://docs.rs#164)        let cl = &mut self.services[idx];
[165](https://docs.rs#165)        self.not_ready.push_back(idx);
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        cl.call(req)
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    }
[168](https://docs.rs#168)}
[169](https://docs.rs#169)

[182](https://docs.rs#182)    }

# Steer in tower::steer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower/*/tower/steer/struct.Steer.html

`pub struct Steer<S, F, Req> { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`steer`## Expand description

[ Steer](https://docs.rs/struct.Steer.html) manages a list of

[s which all handle the same type of request.](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`An example use case is a sharded service. It accepts new requests, then:

- Determines, via the provided `Picker``Service`
- Waits (in `Service::poll_ready`*all*services to be ready.
- Calls the correct `Service`

Note that [ Steer](https://docs.rs/struct.Steer.html) must wait for all services to be ready since it can’t know ahead of time
which

[the next message will arrive for, and is unwilling to buffer items indefinitely. This will cause head-of-line blocking unless paired with a](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[that does buffer items indefinitely, and thus always returns](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[. For example, wrapping each component service with a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/task/poll/enum.Poll.html#variant.Ready)

`Poll::Ready`[with a high enough limit (the maximum number of concurrent requests) will prevent head-of-line blocking in](https://docs.rs/buffer/struct.Buffer.html)

`Buffer`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Steer.html)

[60](#60)            self.inner = match self.inner {
[61](#61)                Inner::Service(ref mut svc) => {
[62](#62)                    if let Poll::Ready(r) = svc.as_mut().expect("illegal state").poll_ready(cx) {
[63](#63)                        return Poll::Ready(r.map_err(Into::into));
[64](#64)                    }
[65](#65)
[66](#66)                    let svc = svc.take().expect("illegal state");
[67](#67)                    let rx =
[68](#68)                        tokio::spawn(svc.ready_oneshot().map_err(Into::into).in_current_span());
[69](#69)                    Inner::Future(rx)
[70](#70)                }
[71](#71)                Inner::Future(ref mut fut) => {
[72](#72)                    let svc = ready!(Pin::new(fut).poll(cx))??;
[73](#73)                    Inner::Service(Some(svc))
[74](#74)                }
[75](#75)            }
[76](#76)        }
[77](#77)    }
[78](#78)
[79](#79)    fn call(&mut self, request: Req) -> Self::Future {
[80](#80)        match self.inner {
[81](#81)            Inner::Service(Some(ref mut svc)) => {
[82](#82)                ResponseFuture::new(svc.call(request).map_err(Into::into))
[83](#83)            }
[84](#84)            _ => unreachable!("poll_ready must be called"),
[85](#85)        }
[86](#86)    }

[1](https://docs.rs#1)use std::convert::Infallible;

[4](https://docs.rs#4)
[5](https://docs.rs#5)/// A [`MakeService`] that produces services by cloning an inner service.
[6](https://docs.rs#6)///
[7](https://docs.rs#7)/// [`MakeService`]: super::MakeService
[8](https://docs.rs#8)///
[9](https://docs.rs#9)/// # Example
[10](https://docs.rs#10)///
[11](https://docs.rs#11)/// ```

[13](https://docs.rs#13)/// # use std::pin::Pin;
[14](https://docs.rs#14)/// # use std::convert::Infallible;
[15](https://docs.rs#15)/// use std::future::{Ready, ready};
[16](https://docs.rs#16)/// use tower::make::{MakeService, Shared};
[17](https://docs.rs#17)/// use tower::buffer::Buffer;
[18](https://docs.rs#18)/// use tower::Service;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)///
[20](https://docs.rs#20)/// // An example connection type
[21](https://docs.rs#21)/// struct Connection {}
[22](https://docs.rs#22)///
[23](https://docs.rs#23)/// // An example request type
[24](https://docs.rs#24)/// struct Request {}
[25](https://docs.rs#25)///
[26](https://docs.rs#26)/// // An example response type
[27](https://docs.rs#27)/// struct Response {}
[28](https://docs.rs#28)///
[29](https://docs.rs#29)/// // Some service that doesn't implement `Clone`
[30](https://docs.rs#30)/// struct MyService;
[31](https://docs.rs#31)///
[32](https://docs.rs#32)/// impl Service<Request> for MyService {
[33](https://docs.rs#33)///     type Response = Response;
[34](https://docs.rs#34)///     type Error = Infallible;
[35](https://docs.rs#35)///     type Future = Ready<Result<Response, Infallible>>;
[36](https://docs.rs#36)///
[37](https://docs.rs#37)///     fn poll_ready(&mut self, _cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
[38](https://docs.rs#38)///         Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
[39](https://docs.rs#39)///     }
[40](https://docs.rs#40)///
[41](https://docs.rs#41)///     fn call(&mut self, req: Request) -> Self::Future {
[42](https://docs.rs#42)///         ready(Ok(Response {}))
[43](https://docs.rs#43)///     }
[44](https://docs.rs#44)/// }
[45](https://docs.rs#45)///
[46](https://docs.rs#46)/// // Example function that runs a service by accepting new connections and using
[47](https://docs.rs#47)/// // `Make` to create new services that might be bound to the connection.
[48](https://docs.rs#48)/// //
[49](https://docs.rs#49)/// // This is similar to what you might find in hyper.
[50](https://docs.rs#50)/// async fn serve_make_service<Make>(make: Make)
[51](https://docs.rs#51)/// where
[52](https://docs.rs#52)///     Make: MakeService<Connection, Request>
[53](https://docs.rs#53)/// {
[54](https://docs.rs#54)///     // ...
[55](https://docs.rs#55)/// }
[56](https://docs.rs#56)///
[57](https://docs.rs#57)/// # async {
[58](https://docs.rs#58)/// // Our service
[59](https://docs.rs#59)/// let svc = MyService;
[60](https://docs.rs#60)///
[61](https://docs.rs#61)/// // Make it `Clone` by putting a channel in front
[62](https://docs.rs#62)/// let buffered = Buffer::new(svc, 1024);
[63](https://docs.rs#63)///
[64](https://docs.rs#64)/// // Convert it into a `MakeService`
[65](https://docs.rs#65)/// let make = Shared::new(buffered);
[66](https://docs.rs#66)///
[67](https://docs.rs#67)/// // Run the service and just ignore the `Connection`s as `MyService` doesn't need them
[68](https://docs.rs#68)/// serve_make_service(make).await;
[69](https://docs.rs#69)/// # };
[70](https://docs.rs#70)/// ```
[71](https://docs.rs#71)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
